title: Minimum Operations to Make the Integer Zero
summary: Given integers num1 and num2, perform operations by choosing an integer i in the range [0, 60] to subtract 2^i + num2 from num1.
statement: Given integers num1 and num2, perform operations by choosing an integer i in the range [0, 60] to subtract 2^i + num2 from num1. Determine the minimum number of operations to reach num1 = 0, or return -1 if impossible.
constraints: One operation chooses any nonnegative i and subtracts 2^i+num2 from num1.
Return the minimum operations needed to make num1 zero, or -1 when impossible.
The chosen exponent may differ between operations.
hints: After k operations, the selected powers must sum to num1-k*num2.
A positive integer can be written as k powers of two exactly when bit_count(value)<=k<=value.
Test k from one through sixty and return the first satisfying both bounds.
Set bits give the minimum terms; repeatedly splitting a power doubles one term into two and reaches every count up to the all-ones maximum.
editorial: Set bits give the minimum terms; repeatedly splitting a power doubles one term into two and reaches every count up to the all-ones maximum.

tests.explanation: Three operations choosing powers that sum to nine subtract 9-6=3 in total.
Every operation subtracts more than the remaining positive target, so reaching zero is impossible.
